domain_label: Sweater Vertical — Ex-Factory Conversion Cost Stack & Make-vs-Buy
purpose: A method for computing the honest ex-factory CONVERSION cost of one Ludhiana-made fully-fashioned sweater article-by-article — the ten cost lines, the boundary that separates this number from landed cost, COGS-to-stock and the D2C P&L, the two-number frame in which yarn sets the cost LEVEL while the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate sets the UNCERTAINTY, the make-vs-buy boundary that same rate decides, and the dye-lot MOQ plus working-capital trap that size the real launch cheque — without ever fabricating the missing per-piece rate or presenting any cost band as a quote.
assumptions: no live mandi or job-worker quote stands behind any figure; every cost band is a labeled estimate carrying the literal word estimate with a confidence, never a quote and never fake-precise, and the genuinely-missing Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate stays [UNKNOWN] and is named as the segment blocker, never invented

the boundary is ex-factory conversion cost per garment (full yarn through overhead/job-worker margin), explicitly not landed cost, not COGS-to-stock, and not the D2C P&L; freight, US duty, CAC, returns and contribution margin live downstream in T9/T7
yarn is ~50-60% of the knit-garment stack anchored on Vardhman FY20 raw-material = 54% of revenue [FACT], giving ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater [ESTIMATE, MED]; this sets the level reliably

the venture is a small AI-designed D2C capsule buying knit+link+finish as job-work into the Ludhiana mesh on bought-dyed stock-shade yarn, owning only design+brand+US import; the make-vs-buy verdict began as reconstructed-consensus across T1/T2/T3 and was then CROSS-EXAMINED by the independent adversarial analyst-B memo, so it is a TESTED A/B conclusion carrying explicit flip-conditions (B2-over-B1 most likely, decidable now), not an un-challenged default; the article bands' PRECISION nonetheless stays blocked by the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate and must be read as wide labelled illustrations, never quotes

EPF 12% + ESI 3.25% ~= 15%+ compliance loading is applied only to the on-roll labour-bearing portion (sampling, in-house finishing/QC), not the whole stack; off-paper friction/speed-money and inverted-duty/GST drag are real mechanisms whose per-unit amounts are [UNKNOWN] and are not added to the per-garment stack
exclusions: landed cost — ocean freight, US duty (cotton 6110.20 ~7% / wool 6110.11 ~16%), insurance, broker, drayage, financing (all T9)
the D2C P&L — CAC, returns, payment fees, AOV, contribution margin and the LTV:CAC viability test (T7/T9); contribution margin after CAC, not factory cost, decides viability
stating a fabricated point value for the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate, the off-paper friction magnitude, or the inverted-duty drag magnitude as a per-unit COGS line
yarn fibre/count selection and the anti-pill quality spec (T2), machine buy/build economics beyond the make-vs-buy boundary (T3), and the quality/thread-checker device (T5)
any owned-dyehouse cost model — dyeing is the highest-regulatory-risk node and is out of bounds as an owned step by standing verdict

glossary.definition: The boundary this KB computes: full (dyed) yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack + QC + EPF/ESI on on-roll labour + overhead/job-worker margin, ending at the factory gate; explicitly NOT landed cost, NOT COGS-to-stock, and NOT the D2C P&L.

The structural reduction of the segment: yarn sets the LEVEL of the stack (well-anchored at ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater) while the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate sets the UNCERTAINTY (~25-45% of the conversion subtotal) and the same missing rate decides make-vs-buy.

The Ludhiana per-piece charge to knit the fully-fashioned panels and to link them loop-to-loop; no reliable public figure exists (T1 Open Q#1, T3 Open Q#2); it is the single highest-leverage missing number, held [UNKNOWN] and never fabricated, and one on-the-ground quote run unblocks the whole segment.

The binding honesty label on every cost/price/throughput/MOQ band here: a reasoned [ESTIMATE] with method, basis and confidence, never a live mandi or job-worker quote and never fake-precise; bands stand, points do not.

EPF 12% + ESI 3.25% ~= 15%+ applied only to the on-roll labour-bearing portion the brand carries directly (sampling, in-house finishing/QC), never the whole stack; in a subcontract model most of it lands on the job-worker and the competitive-gap magnitude vs an off-roll competitor stays [UNKNOWN].

Planned discretionary-gate cost described as MECHANISM, never as a named-party accusation; episodic and amortising to near-zero per garment at capsule volume, every amount [UNKNOWN] by design, NOT added to the per-garment stack — a T9 cash/approval line.

Acrylic (MMF) input tax exceeding output tax traps working capital in slow refunds; a cash-conversion-cycle cost (T9), magnitude [UNKNOWN], NOT a clean per-garment COGS add — named here, quantified in T9.

The binding launch constraint: ~150-500 kg dyed yarn per colour (economic dye-house MOQ ~500-2,000 kg/colour, +20-50% small-batch surcharge below it); at ~300-400 g/sweater, 200 kg ~= 500-650 sweaters of ONE colour, which forces a colour-starved 2-4-colour launch and sizes the first cheque, not the unit cost.

At capsule scale own only design+brand+US import, subcontract knit+link+finish into the Ludhiana job-work mesh, buy yarn in-cluster on bought-dyed stock shades, rent/contract the scarce CAD/flat-knit programmer; in-source a step only at proven repeating volume, linking LAST, never own a dyehouse, never build a machine; a TESTED conclusion [ESTIMATE: judgment, HIGH] — reconstructed-consensus across T1/T2/T3 then cross-examined by the adversarial analyst-B memo, carrying explicit flip-conditions (choose B1/B2/B3 on evidence; B2-over-B1 decidable now).

An external published fully-fashioned-knitwear costing study used ONLY for the per-piece shape (linking ~60% of knitting cost per piece, the labour-heavy seam), [DOWNGRADED] to LOW-MED; Ludhiana labour is cheaper but the pc/operator-day productivity is [UNKNOWN], so it bounds a band and never collapses to a Ludhiana quote.

nodes.definition: Fix the boundary before any figure is computed, because getting it wrong is the most expensive mistake in the segment. This model computes EX-FACTORY CONVERSION COST per garment: full (dyed) yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack, giving a direct-conversion subtotal, plus EPF/ESI loading (~15%+ on the on-roll labour portion only) plus factory overhead / job-worker margin, ending at the factory gate. It is NOT landed cost (freight, US duty cotton 6110.20 ~7% / wool 6110.11 ~16%, insurance, broker, drayage, financing all live in T9), NOT COGS-to-stock, NOT the D2C P&L (CAC, returns, fees, contribution margin are the T7/T9 survival test — contribution margin after CAC, not factory cost, decides viability), and NOT a quote (bands only, by honest necessity). The factory gate is the cheapest, least-decisive part of the journey; cost it honestly, then hand the margin fight downstream.

included: the ex-factory conversion definition (yarn through overhead/margin)
the four things it is not (landed, COGS-to-stock, P&L, quote)
the bands-only honesty necessity
excluded: the landed stack and the P&L themselves

pros.claim: Pinning the boundary first stops the segment's most expensive error: optimising the wrong number
pros.example: refusing to read a $5 ex-factory figure as a margin verdict because CAC and duty are not yet in it

cons.claim: A clean boundary can lull the owner into treating ex-factory as the whole game when the margin fight is downstream
cons.example: over-optimising the loom while CAC quietly governs viability in T7/T9

failure_modes: reading the ex-factory number as landed or as profit
adding T9 freight/duty into the conversion stack and double-counting downstream
acceptance_tests: the boundary states the conversion definition and explicitly names landed cost, COGS-to-stock, P&L and quote as what it is not, with the contribution-margin-after-CAC caveat
revisit_triggers: the T9 landed model changes what sits above the gate
a duty line (cotton/wool 6110) is updated
the venture changes its importer-of-record posture

base.update_signal: the boundary above the factory gate (landed/P&L) or a duty line changes

nodes.definition: Reduce the whole segment to two facts pulling in opposite directions. Yarn sets the LEVEL and it is well-anchored: yarn is ~50-60% of the knit-garment stack (Vardhman FY20 raw material = 54% of revenue [FACT], held at MED, not promoted to a measured cluster average), ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater at ~300-500 g [ESTIMATE, MED] — so the magnitude of the stack is reliable. The knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate sets the UNCERTAINTY and it is [UNKNOWN]: labour (knit/link/finish/check) is ~15-25% of the stack and the knit+LINK lines inside it are ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal with no reliable public figure. The owner takeaway: do not hunt cheaper yarn (small, anchored, not the constraint); get the one number — the rupees/piece to knit and to link — because it halves every band below AND settles the make-vs-buy crossover in one stroke.

included: yarn-sets-the-level vs rate-sets-the-uncertainty split
why yarn is not the constraint
the single-number leverage on both bands and make-vs-buy
excluded: the yarn anchor detail (its own node)

pros.claim: The frame directs effort to the one high-leverage number instead of the anchored, low-leverage one
pros.example: spending a sourcing trip on the rupees/piece knit+link rate rather than chasing a cheaper yarn count

cons.claim: Splitting level from uncertainty can be read as if yarn never matters, when a premium-fibre article is yarn-dominated
cons.example: applying the value/core $1-2.50 level to an A3 merino capsule where yarn swamps the stack

failure_modes: treating yarn as the constraint and over-optimising it
forgetting that the same missing rate decides make-vs-buy, not just the bands
acceptance_tests: the frame states yarn sets the anchored level (~$1-2.50, 54% anchor) and the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate sets the uncertainty (~25-45% of conversion) and is the single highest-leverage number
revisit_triggers: a live knit+link quote run lands and collapses the uncertainty
the yarn-share anchor is re-measured

nodes.definition: Carry the load-bearing anchor that fixes the LEVEL of the stack. In garment terms that is ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater at ~300-500 g [ESTIMATE, MED, carried from T2]. The anchor is reliable enough that the magnitude of the stack is not the open question; the premium-fibre rows (lambswool/merino/cashmere) are order-of-magnitude only and need an importer quote before any margin use.

nodes.definition: Name the single [UNKNOWN] that blocks precision across the whole segment: the Ludhiana per-piece rate to KNIT the fully-fashioned panels and to LINK them loop-to-loop. No reliable public figure exists (confirmed across T1 Open Q#1, T3 Open Q#2, and the cost-model search); it is carried verbatim as the single highest-value missing number and is never fabricated. The knit+LINK lines are ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal — the part that cannot be priced — so the precision of the stack is blocked at exactly this one input. Worse, the same rate is the make-vs-buy crossover: owning knitting beats subcontracting only when the owned per-piece cost at the brand's utilisation falls below the subcontract rate, which cannot be located until the subcontract rate is known. One on-the-ground quote run from 2-3 job-workers (rupees/piece at 7GG and 12GG, 300 g and 400 g pullovers) collapses both lines to [ESTIMATE, MED], halves every band, and settles the crossover — the highest-leverage data acquisition in the segment. On-the-ground only; never invent it.

nodes.definition: Cost line 2: the per-piece charge to knit the fully-fashioned panels into shape on a computerised flat machine, subcontracted into the Ludhiana job-work mesh. With linking, this line is ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal — the precision-blocking part of the stack.

nodes.definition: Cost line 3: the per-piece charge to LINK the fully-fashioned panels edge-to-edge loop-to-loop — the eyesight-intensive, hand-skilled, piece-rate seam that defines a quality FF sweater and SETS the small line's daily capacity (the linker, not the knitter, caps throughput). This is the second [UNKNOWN]-rate line: the Ludhiana per-piece link rate has no reliable public figure and is never fabricated. The FF-costing cross-check puts linking at ~US$0.45/pc at ~15 pc/operator-day (~60% of knitting cost per piece) as SHAPE-only [DOWNGRADED], consistent with the linker-sets-the-ceiling logic. With knitting, ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal. Linking is the step in-sourced LAST in the make-vs-buy ladder because it is both the throughput bottleneck and the hardest skill to re-hire.

nodes.definition: Cost line 4: finishing — wash/scour, soften, anti-pill, steam/press/board, mend — the job-work steps that turn a harsh off-machine panel into retail product. A cheap line in dollar terms [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED], but for the A2 acrylic value driver the anti-pill sub-step is mandatory, not optional: the article's margin lives or dies on the anti-pill finish surviving ICI Pilling-Box grade >=3-4 after a home wash, and if that line is cut to save cents it returns as the #1 return driver and destroys the contribution margin downstream. Supplied by the mesh as job-work; optionally one cheap used press is owned for sampling only.

nodes.definition: Cost line 5: trims, labels and packing — care + brand + size labels, polybag, hangtag, and the carton share. The care/fibre-composition label is also a duty-and-compliance surface: the blend ratio printed on it must match the PO tolerance because blend drift is both a quiet supplier cost-down and a US duty-misdeclaration exposure for the brand as importer of record.

nodes.definition: Cost line 6: QC / checking — in-line plus final AQL checking and a mend allowance. A modest line [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED], grouped with trims into the ~$0.8-1.8 combined allowance. Posture is contractual AQL sampling plus a reject rule, not in-house metrology.

nodes.definition: The clean hand-off that composes the whole KB toward T9, the synthesis the segment builds to. Take the per-article bands (A1 ~$4-9, A2 ~$3.5-8, A3 ~$6-22+) as the ex-factory INPUT, apply the volume-tier adjustment (small-batch dye surcharge + thin per-style setup at the brand's ACTUAL launch MOQ, which pushes micro-volume cost above the bands), then hand a single labelled ex-factory band to T9, which stacks freight + duty (~7% cotton 6110.20 / ~16% wool 6110.11) + insurance + broker + drayage + financing and runs the landed cost plus the CAC/contribution test. T9 owns whether the venture makes money; T4 owns only the honest factory-gate number and the cash it ties up. One job-worker quote run (per-piece knit+link rate, plus the FOB price+MOQ half for the B1-vs-B2 trade study) converts the whole illustration into a real model and locates the make-vs-buy crossover — the highest-leverage action in the segment. The make-vs-buy verdict has been cross-examined by analyst-B, so it hands off as a TESTED conclusion with flip-conditions; the bands' width remains [UNKNOWN]-rate-blocked, so T9 must treat them as wide labelled inputs until a quote run lands.

priority_rationale: The boundary and the two-number frame come first because every figure is meaningless until the ex-factory gate is fixed and the anchored yarn LEVEL is separated from the [UNKNOWN]-rate UNCERTAINTY; the ten cost lines and the shape-only cross-check next, because they are the terms the model sums and the only honest way to bound the missing knit+LINK rate; the summation formula and the three per-article bands then apply that to concrete articles as labelled illustrations; the make-vs-buy ladder, the dye-lot MOQ first cheque (carrying the per-style setup uplift) and the working-capital trap follow, because they are the launch-sizing constraints larger than the unit cost itself; and the stepped volume curve and the T9 hand-off come last because they compose every upstream output into a volume-adjusted ex-factory band that feeds the landed and CAC/contribution test T9 owns.
